```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B has stronger willingness-to-pay evidence. Ello charges $14.99/mo despite a fully free Khan Academy Kids, which shows paid products survive next to free ones in this category. Mentava at $500/mo, even with backlash, shows a high ceiling. A's only payment evidence is a $3/mo competitor (Maskwire) that bundles this feature as one of six tools, so there is no evidence anyone pays for it standalone.",
    "B's demand quotes come from parents who have already spent money or effort on tutors and apps and are still unsatisfied. A's demand quotes describe a mail-client annoyance, with no sign that the people complaining would pay to fix it.",
    "A's own brief undercuts its whitespace. At least five live competitors ship the exact feature, several on free tiers. A free open-source Thunderbird extension already solves the client-side case, which is the plugin route A's 'case for' proposes as its easiest build.",
    "Price headroom matters even for a first customer. B's price is 4-5x A's ceiling. A's Reddit CPC of $0.50-$4 is roughly equal to one month of revenue, so A's acquisition math is worse than B's CPI of $2.50-$5 against a $15/mo price.",
    "B's risks are real but mostly one-time or bounded. A COPPA legal consult and a narrow niche can address the consent and efficacy concerns. B also has an organic channel: parenting subreddits where parents ask for app recommendations. That channel's cost is unsourced, so it counts only as a weak plus."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence. The three forum quotes (Zoho, Apple, Microsoft) come from users of business and domain-alias setups, such as an admin wanting replies 'from info'. They are not from the privacy-conscious many-alias prosumers A names as its payer, and none carries any willingness-to-pay signal. They show a mismatch with the target segment, not demand for a paid standalone product.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. A is cheaper to build and has lighter regulatory burden, which counts for something under a 90-day deadline. B's COPPA obligations, trust-building, and free incumbents could easily delay a first sale. B wins mainly because A's brief shows no evidence of standalone willingness to pay and documents near-total competitive coverage. B's organic-channel cost and state-law specifics are unsourced and were treated as missing."
}
```
